summary:
I’ve failed to answer your letter of December 27 up to now because of seri­ ous illness (I’ve had first the London flu and then double pneumonia, right through Christmas and on down the weeks to whatever holiday it is we just had). Even my typewriter, as you can see from the several inkings, has broken down during this long period; I think there’s a spider living in it now, or maybe it’s Bob Heinlein. Anyhow, thank you for asking me to speak. My only question is: is it too late for me to participate? Is it all over? I would like to very much. Well, maybe one more question, which is about transportation. We have no car. In fact we have no phone and no TV set either, but in this matter it’s a car that counts. Any help possible from you on that7 This flu-pneumonia really almost did me in. I had to cancel on all speaking stuff everywhere throughout the known world and parts even unknown, at least to me (like at small high schools south of here). My stamina is still low—and this f—g typewriter still isn’t inking—but anyhow I’d like to do it, provided of course that if I die between now and March 31 you won’t be mad at me. How, really, can you be mad at someone who’s dead as well as someone whose typewriter types like this and he has to earn a living on that very same typewriter not only for himself but for his girlfriend and her unwed baby (that doesn’t sound right) and their pink cat and god knows what else?
